commands_joint.label: Joint Origin
commands_joint.params: name?, occurrence?: id|name (default: from the pick, or the named face's component), face: [x,y,z] | "<name>" (centre of a planar face) | circle: [x,y,z] | "<name>" (centre of a round end: a point on its wall or rim, the end's centre, or the round face's name as model.faces lists it) | edge: [x,y,z] (a point on an edge of a planar face: the edge's middle, z out of the face, y into it; on?: [x,y,z] a point on the face (default: the larger planar face beside the edge); corner?: [x,y,z] near one end: the corner there, x and y along its two edges into the face; found again by name, so it follows the face as it changes size) | point: [x,y,z], z?: [x,y,z]; body?: the named face's body; end?: "<name>" (a circle's end: the face across its rim there; default the end nearer the pick); x?: [x,y,z] (a direction, world) | "<face name>" | {face: [x,y,z]} (the frame's x: a direction, a plane's normal, or the way to another hole's axis; keeps a round origin's turn; a point's x is a direction, laid square to its z, default: chosen from z alone). Faces are kept by name: the origin follows its face, and a circle its end, when the design changes

commands_joint.label: Joint
commands_joint.params: type: rigid|revolute|slider|cylindrical|pin_slot|planar|ball, or a relation: parallel|perpendicular|angle|point_on_plane|point_on_line|line_on_plane (ties only some directions or points, made where the parts are; several between two parts add up); a, b: joint origins ({occurrence, face|circle|edge|point: [x,y,z] in world, or face|circle: "<face name>"; z? for a point, end?, x? as joint.origin} | origin name); values?: [angles in deg or expressions, distances]; limits?: [[min, max] | null…]; flip?: bool (default false: the origins are mated, b's z against a's as two faces meet; true: b's z along a's, so two origins given at one point with the same z stay as they are); offset?: mm or an expression; angle?: deg or an expression (an angle relation's tilt from mated; for other joints the default is none, or a half turn where that turns b less, so faces that already meet stay as they are); name?; quiet?: bool (leave out dof and fixed). An expression (text) is kept with the joint and worked out again whenever the design changes, so the joint follows the parameters it names; a joint whose expression no longer works out (a parameter deleted) is left out of the solve with the reason in its errors

commands_joint.label: As-Built Joint
commands_joint.params: type, a: occurrence, b: occurrence (stay where they are); at?: joint origin (default: b's origin) — the joint's frame; one on a or b is kept on its face or hole there, so the joint follows it as the design changes; name?; limits?: [[min, max] | null…]; quiet?: bool

commands_joint.label: Rigid Group
commands_joint.params: occurrences: [ids or names] (move together, as they are)

commands_joint.label: Drive Joints
commands_joint.params: joint: id|name; value | values: [angles in deg or expressions, distances] (values not given keep theirs; a value driven drops the expression joint.create gave it; clamped to the limits; the other joints of a closed loop follow, and the motion stops where the loop can no longer close → stopped_by_loop); quiet?: bool (leave out dof and fixed) → values: [{name, value, unit: deg|mm, limits}] as joint.list gives them; moved: whether any occurrence moved; reason: why the joint can move nothing (suppressed, its origins lost, or its chain joined to nothing grounded → unconnected: the occurrence named)

commands_joint.label: Reach Point
commands_joint.params: occurrence: id|name; point: [x,y,z] (where its point goes, world); at?: [x,y,z] (its point, in the world where it is now; default: the centre of          its bodies' box); z?: [x,y,z] (the way its axis then points); axis?: [x,y,z] (that axis, in the world now; default: its own z); joints?: [ids          or names] (only these move toward the point; the other joints of a closed loop they are in follow); quiet?: bool; continuous?: bool (a frame          of a drag: the answer says continuous, and the app's command line doesn't echo it). Moves the values of the joints          on its chain from where they are to the nearest pose, within their limits, through motion links, keeping closed loops closed as joint.drive does          (contact sets are not checked) → reached; error_mm (and error_deg with z): how close it got; point: where its point is; values: [{joint, name,          values}] of the joints that moved, as joint.list gives them; moved; stopped_by_limit: [{joint, value, limit: min|max}]: the limits it rests on          short of the point; stopped_by_loop: {joint}: the closed loop that stopped it (its chain alone gets closer); reason: why nothing can move

commands_joint.label: Motion Link
commands_joint.params: a, b: joints; ratio (b = ratio · a + offset): b's units per a's (mm per deg for an angle driving a distance); offset?: in b's units (deg for an angle, mm for a distance, or an expression); ia?, ib?: value indices (default 0)

commands_joint.label: Gear
commands_joint.params: a, b: joints that turn (revolute), b driven by a; ra, rb: the gears' pitch radii (or tooth counts): mm, an expression, or {circle: [x,y,z], occurrence?}: the round face there, its radius (read again whenever the design changes, so the ratio follows edits); internal?: bool (one is a ring gear: both turn the same way; by default b turns the other way); reverse?: bool; link?: index (replace that motion link) → link, ratio (b's degrees per a's); b keeps where it is, also when the link replaces another (at the current pose)

commands_joint.label: Rack and Pinion
commands_joint.params: a, b: a joint that turns (revolute: the pinion) and one that slides (slider: the rack), in either order, b driven by a; radius: the pinion's pitch radius (mm, an expression, or {circle: [x,y,z], occurrence?}): the rack travels radius × the turn in radians; reverse?: bool; link?: index (replace that motion link) → link, ratio (mm per degree, or degrees per mm); b keeps where it is, also when the link replaces another (at the current pose)

commands_joint.label: Screw
commands_joint.params: joint: a cylindrical joint (its turn drives its travel) | a, b: a joint that turns and one that slides, b driven by a; pitch: travel per turn (mm or an expression); reverse?: bool (a left-hand thread); link?: index (replace that motion link) → link, ratio (mm per degree, or degrees per mm); b keeps where it is, also when the link replaces another (at the current pose)

commands_joint.label: Cam
commands_joint.params: a: the cam's joint (revolute); b: the follower's joint, a slider (a translating follower) or a revolute (an oscillating one),          b driven by a; profile: {sketch: id|name, index?: the profile (default: the largest)} | {edges: [[x,y,z]…] (points on edges of          the cam's bodies forming one closed loop, world), occurrence?}: the cam's outline, in a plane square to its axis, read again          whenever the design changes; follower?: knife|roller|flat (default knife; flat: a face square to a slider's line); radius?: the          roller's radius (mm, an expression or {circle: [x,y,z], occurrence?}: the roller's round face, which is its tip too); tip?: a          joint origin where the follower touches: its knife's point or its roller's centre, such as {circle: [x,y,z]} on the roller          (needed for an oscillating follower; a translating one's line runs through it, by default along its slider's axis); flip?: bool (ride the cam from the other side          than the one the follower is on now); link?: index (replace that motion link) → link, lift: {min, max, rise, unit} (b's travel          over a turn of the cam), reverse (the side it rides from), follower_offset (mm: how far a translating follower's line passes          from the cam's axis); b keeps where it is, also when the link replaces another (at the current pose)

commands_joint.label: Joint Limits
commands_joint.params: joint; index?: value index (default 0); min?, max? (omit both to clear)

commands_joint.label: Edit Joint
commands_joint.params: joint; type?, flip?, offset?, angle? (a number, or an expression the joint then follows), suppressed?, name?

commands_joint.label: Delete Joint
commands_joint.params: joint: id|name (or origin: name, link: index)

commands_joint.label: List Joints
commands_joint.params: → joints (type, occurrences, values, limits; expressions: {offset?, angle?, values?} when they were typed as expressions), origins, links, degrees of freedom, conflicts, floating: [{occurrences, joints}] (joint chains joined to nothing grounded: the solver places none of them, so driving them moves nothing)

commands_joint.label: Inspect Joint
commands_joint.params: joint?: id|name (default: every joint) → joints: [{id, name, type, suppressed, visible, flip, offset (mm), angle (deg), values: as joint.list gives them, dofs, expressions?: {offset?, angle?, values?}, a, b: {occurrence, occurrence_name, component, component_name, path (occurrence names from the top, `/` between), snap (as saved: type, pick, face, end, edge, corner, x, point, z, in the component's coordinates), references: [{role: face|end|x|edge|corner, name, role_in_feature?: (top, side:c1…), feature?: {id, name, type} (the feature that made the face; error when it is gone), sketch?: {id, name, curve, curve_type} (a face swept from a sketch curve), faces?: [an edge's two faces], unverified?: a name saved before exact names}], resolves, frame?: {origin, z, x} in the world, error?: why the origin is lost}, links: [{index, role: driver|driven, …as joint.list}], errors, conflicts}] (reads only: nothing changes)

commands_joint.label: Solve Joints
commands_joint.params: re-place the occurrences from the joints → conflicts, errors, dof

commands_joint.label: Sweep Joint
commands_joint.params: joint: id|name; from, to: its value the sweep runs between (degrees for angles, mm for distances, or expressions); index? (which value, default 0); step? (between samples, in the joint's unit; default: fine enough that no part passes through another between two); refine?: mm (the first contact is bisected until no part moves more than this between the last clear value and the touching one; default 0.01); occurrences?: [ids or names] (checked against each other; default every occurrence), with against?: [ids or names] (the parts that stay: each of `occurrences` only against these), or contact_sets?: true (the pairs of the design's contact sets); report_gaps?: bool (the nearest gap at every sample, default false); apply?: bool (leave the design where the sweep stopped; default false: the design is not changed) → stopped_at (the last value clear of contact, or where a loop or limit stopped it; null: it reached `to`), stopped_by: {a, b, at: [x,y,z] (where they touch, world)} | "loop" | "limit" | null, samples: [{value, min_gap_mm?, pair?}], min_gap? (report_gaps: {part: {mm, at_value, to}}, the nearest each part came to another), unit, gap_method ("mesh": distances between the tessellations), gap_tolerance_mm (how far those can be off: 0 when every face is flat), pairs (checked), touching_at_start: [[a, b]] (pairs already touching at `from`, such as parts joined face to face or a door on its frame: these stop it only once they pass into each other deeper than they start), applied. The parts are tested at the samples and through the bisection; the motion is on a copy (closed loops follow, contact sets do not stop it)

commands_motion.label: Motion Link
commands_motion.params: a, b: joints; ratio (b = ratio · a + offset): b's units per a's (mm per deg for an angle driving a distance); offset?: in b's units (deg for an angle, mm for a distance, or an expression); ia?, ib?: value indices (default 0)

commands_motion.label: Motion Study
commands_motion.params: name?; study? (edit an existing one); steps? (timeline length, default 100); keys: [{joint, index?, points: [[step, value], …]}] (values: degrees for angles, mm for distances, or expressions)

commands_motion.label: Play Motion Study
commands_motion.params: study: id|name; step (0…steps) — sets the joints to the study's values there (contact sets stop them); quiet?: bool (positions of only the occurrences that moved) → values: [{joint, values: [{name, value, unit}]}], positions, moved: whether any occurrence moved, unmoved: [{joint, name, reason}] (keyed joints that can move nothing, such as a chain joined to nothing grounded)

commands_motion.label: Export Motion Study
commands_motion.params: study; samples? (default steps + 1); path? (.json or .csv) → occurrence positions per step (the design is not changed)

commands_motion.label: Export Motion Animation
commands_motion.params: study: id|name, or joint: id|name with from and to (degrees for angles, mm for distances, or expressions) and index?;          path: a .gif file, or a folder for PNG frames (frame-0001.png, frame-0002.png, …); samples? (frames, 2…1000; default the          study's steps + 1, or 100); width?, height? (16…4096 pixels, default 800 × 500); camera?: {target, yaw, pitch, roll?,          distance, fov?, up?} (ui.camera's reply; fields left out keep the default view: view.apply's camera, or the home view          framing the model); fps? (1…50, default 20); grid?, axes? (default true: the ground grid and the origin's axes) - draws the study as it plays, or the joint as it is driven, with the headless          renderer → path, format, frames, width, height, fps (GIF), bytes, renderer, stopped_at, stopped_by_loop,          stopped_by_contact (the design is not changed)

commands_motion.label: Motion Trace
commands_motion.params: occurrence: id|name, or an occurrence path [ids] (an instance inside sub-assemblies); point: [x,y,z] world point on it, where it is placed now; study: id|name, or joint: id|name with from and to (degrees for angles, mm for distances, or expressions) and index? (which value, default 0); samples? (2…500, default the study's steps + 1, or 100) - the point's path as the study plays or the joint is driven, closed loops following → points: [[x,y,z]…] world positions, samples (taken), stopped_at (the sample where the motion stopped short; the trace ends there), stopped_by_loop, stopped_by_contact (the design is not changed)

commands_motion.label: Keep Motion Trace
commands_motion.params: occurrence: id|name, or an occurrence path [ids] (an instance inside sub-assemblies); point: [x,y,z] world point on it, where it is placed now; study: id|name, or joint: id|name with from and to (degrees for angles, mm for distances, or expressions) and index? (which value, default 0); samples? (2…500, default the study's steps + 1, or 100) - the point's path as the study plays or the joint is driven, closed loops following; name? (default Motion TraceN) - keeps the trace as a 3D sketch spline through its points (a new sketch with 3D Sketch on, in the root component, where no joint moves it; a fixed curve, it does not follow later changes) → sketch, name, curves, points

commands_motion.label: Plot Motion Study
commands_motion.params: study: id|name; joints?: [id|name] (default: every joint that moves); occurrence? and point? (a point of a part to follow, as motion.trace takes them); samples? (3…1000, default the study's steps + 1); duration?: seconds the whole study takes, 0.001 or more (velocities and accelerations then per second, else per step) → step: [the study step of each sample], time?: [s], joints: [{joint, name, index, dof, unit, value, velocity, acceleration, velocity_unit, acceleration_unit}] (degrees for angles, mm for distances; angles unwrapped), point?: {occurrence, position: [[x,y,z]…], velocity, acceleration (vectors), speed, acceleration_norm, unit, velocity_unit, acceleration_unit}, samples (taken), stopped_at, stopped_by_loop, stopped_by_contact. The study plays as motion.play plays it, each sample driven from the one before, on a copy (the design is not changed); velocities and accelerations are finite differences between samples (central, one-sided at the ends)

commands_motion.label: Motion Interference
commands_motion.params: study: id|name; occurrences?: [ids or names] (two or more, checked against each other; default every occurrence), with against?: [ids or names] (then each of `occurrences` is checked only against these, such as an arm against the parts it must miss), or contact_sets?: true (the pairs of the design's contact sets); samples? (2…1000, default the study's steps + 1) → collisions: [{a, b, first_step, last_step, steps: [[from, to]…] (the step ranges where they overlap), depth_mm (how far into each other, the most at deepest_step), volume_mm3 (their overlap there; null when it was not cheap to work out)}], clear, pairs (checked), samples (taken), truncated (the work budget ran out; checked_to: the last step checked), stopped_at, stopped_by_loop. The study plays as motion.play plays it but contact sets do not stop it, on a copy (the design is not changed). Parts are tested at the samples only: one that passes wholly through another between two samples is missed
